title: Attendance and completion in a hospital group pain self-management programme: an implementation study of three adaptations
subtitle: RE-AIM and CFIR guided evaluation of an evening group, a hybrid option and an orientation call
statement: A hospital pain clinic runs an eight-week group self-management programme, but only 41 percent of people who start complete six or more sessions, most dropouts happen early, and the waiting list is seven months. Working people, people who depend on public transport and people who speak Portuguese or Tagalog at home appear to leave most often. The clinic plans three adaptations in 2027 and needs to learn why attendance is low and whether the adaptations improve reach and completion without weakening the programme's benefit.
whoAffected: Adults with chronic back pain, fibromyalgia or widespread pain referred to the programme, the physiotherapist, psychologist and nurse practitioner who run it, and people on the waiting list.
whatHurts: People who leave early lose the programme's benefit and their places are lost to others waiting seven months; the clinic cannot see who leaves or why because outcomes are collected only at the first and last session.
currentPractice: Daytime groups of ten to twelve, eight weekly sessions, questionnaires at the first and last session only, and no follow-up of people who stop attending.
whyNow: Planned adaptations in 2027, a seven-month waiting list and a completion rate the clinic considers too low.
constraints: No research funding; staff time within the clinic's existing budget; outcome questionnaires are collected only at the first and last session; any change to staff hours needs the clinic manager's approval.
patientCenteredGoal: People referred to the programme can attend at a time and in a way that fits their lives and finish it with the skills to manage their pain.
summary: Problem framed as an implementation study of three adaptations to improve reach and completion.
